title: Revise auth header handshake for browser streaming, tool-calls, and OpenAI-compat
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Auth: accept both Bearer and project-scoped tokens for streaming endpoints; introduce X-Redwood-Nonce for ephemeral token handshake; update OpenAI-compat header mappings; CORS fixes for credentialless SSE in browsers.
description: Context: customers embedding streaming chat and function/tool calling in browser contexts reported integration friction when using project-scoped keys and the OpenAI-compatible layer (notably when running without cookies/credentials). This PR standardizes header semantics for both long-lived project/org keys and short-lived scoped tokens, and smooths the handshake for browser streaming (SSE/WebSocket fallback) and tool/function calls. What this does: 1) Accepts both Authorization: Bearer <token> and OpenAI-Api-Key: <token> for legacy clients and maps OpenAI keys to the same auth pipeline; 2) Introduces X-Redwood-Nonce (32-byte base64) as an optional header for ephemeral scoped token handshakes used in browser flows; server validates nonce + signature and invalidates on first use to mitigate replay; 3) Adds X-Redwood-Project: <project-id> header support to allow project-scoped keys to be explicit when a multi-tenant token is used for cross-project routing; 4) Modifies CORS policy for streaming endpoints to allow credentialless SSE from approved domains and adds Vary: Origin to responses; 5) Extends request-signing middleware to accept signed payloads that include X-Redwood-Nonce and OpenAI-compat headers (preserves backwards compatibility with existing signatures); 6) Adds integration tests and end-to-end browser harness that exercises SSE + WebSocket fallback with scoped ephemeral keys. Why: reduces integration surface for customers using OpenAI-compatible SDKs in browser-based chat UIs, prevents token replay for ephemeral tokens, and unblocks tool/function calling from unprivileged front-ends. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind auth.v2.handshake; opt-in for 48h; then gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring. See linked Linear items for telemetry and rollout playbook.
commits: 4 commits: initial handshake design and tests; add nonce generation and validation; extend OpenAI-compat header mapping; update CORS and integration fixtures; fix linting & tests after review.
